entities.summary: Hemming Gadh was a Swedish Roman Catholic priest and Bishop of the Diocese of Linköping, serving from 1505 until his death in 1520. He played a pivotal role in the Swedish Reformation, advocating for Lutheranism and opposing the Catholic Church's authority. Gadh's stance on this issue led to a significant divide within the Swedish clergy and contributed to the eventual establishment of the Lutheran Church of Sweden. His legacy as a champion of religious freedom and a fierce defender of the faith has endured for centuries, shaping the course of Swedish history. In a striking display of conviction, Gadh famously declared, 'God's Word must be spoken, even if the devil himself speaks it,' a sentiment that continues to inspire and provoke to this day.
